findings.title: Candidate recurrence ignores changed source revisions
findings.why_it_matters: A corrected source tree must receive a fresh independent challenge instead of being misrouted to a finding-only oscillation halt.
findings.what_is_wrong: The verifier treated candidate_fingerprint alone as the recurrence key even though that hash intentionally excludes source_rev; materially different source revisions with the same scorecard therefore looked recurrent, while Step 1.6 oscillation is defined around reappearing findings.
findings.leverage_impact: One canonical recurrence key governs every post-correction success candidate.
findings.locality_impact: The fingerprint owner and verifier prose disagreed about whether changed source is recurrent.
findings.metric_signal: Two candidates with different source_rev values produced the same fingerprint and the second was still eligible for a productive challenge.
findings.why_weakens_submission: The documented route can falsely halt after a successful correction, preventing the loop from ever proving terminal success even though the source materially changed.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Pair candidate_fingerprint with source_rev for recurrence, retain candidate_commit_sha only as freshness binding, and executable-spec the pair in candidate_fingerprint.py.

simplification_check.structurally_necessary: Changed source must remain eligible for a fresh terminal challenge.
simplification_check.helpful_simplification: Use the existing fingerprint and source_rev as a pair.
simplification_check.should_not_be_done: Do not add a source-tree digest or another persisted field.
simplification_check.tests_after_fix: Run candidate_fingerprint.py plus the full repository suite.

backlog.title: Bind candidate recurrence to source revision
backlog.why_it_matters: Corrected source must not be mistaken for an unchanged recurring candidate.
